title: Hypothesis Generation Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Research observations, proposed explanations, testable predictions, and evaluation criteria. The Hypothesis Generation Database documents how good hypotheses are born: from observations that do not fit, through proposed explanations, to testable predictions with the criteria that would confirm or kill them. A hypothesis that cannot be tested is a story; each record forces the discipline — observation, explanation, prediction, test, criteria — so ideas become science instead of speculation.

title: Hypothesis Generation Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Hypothesis anatomy: OBSERVATION (the anomaly or pattern, with data) -> EXPLANATION (the proposed mechanism, stated precisely) -> PREDICTIONS (what must be true if the explanation holds — novel predictions score higher than retrodictions) -> TEST (the decisive experiment) -> CRITERIA (numeric thresholds for confirm/refine/refute, set in advance). Virtues: testability (falsifiable), specificity (precise predictions), parsimony (simplest adequate explanation), fruitfulness (suggests new tests), consilience (fits other knowledge). Generation heuristics: anomaly focus (what does current theory get wrong?), analogy (what worked elsewhere?), mechanism sketch (what could produce this?), extreme cases (what happens at the limits?). Evaluation: confirmed (criteria met), refuted (criteria failed — record why), refined (partial — new hypothesis spawned).

Demos execute hypothesis formulation on sample observations, prediction checking, test design, and outcome evaluation.

demo.title: Verification: hypothesis anatomy check
demo.code: const hyp={observation:'audio quantizes worse',explanation:'heavy-tailed features',predictions:['tail clipping recovers accuracy'],test:'clip at p99.9, quantize 8-bit',criteria:'recover >=80% of gap'};const fields=['observation','explanation','predictions','test','criteria'];const complete=fields.every(f=>hyp[f]&&(Array.isArray(hyp[f])?hyp[f].length>0:hyp[f].length>0));J({complete});assert(complete,'hypothesis');

title: Hypothesis Generation Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: anatomy test (all fields present and non-vacuous); derivation test (predictions logically follow); criteria test (thresholds numeric and pre-set); status test (no 'confirmed' without evidence). Limitations: quality of hypotheses depends on the observations; evaluation needs real experiments; the database structures thinking, it does not guarantee truth. Every record carries its status and evidence.

demo.title: Verification: trade-off scoring and sensitivity
demo.code: const opts={A:{perf:9,rel:6,simple:5},B:{perf:6,rel:9,simple:8}};const w={perf:0.5,rel:0.3,simple:0.2};function score(o){return o.perf*w.perf+o.rel*w.rel+o.simple*w.simple;}const sA=score(opts.A),sB=score(opts.B);const w2={perf:0.3,rel:0.5,simple:0.2};function score2(o){return o.perf*w2.perf+o.rel*w2.rel+o.simple*w2.simple;}const flip=score2(opts.B)>score2(opts.A);J({sA:+sA.toFixed(2),sB:+sB.toFixed(2),flip});assert(sA>sB&&flip,'tradeoff');

title: Hypothesis Generation Database — Beginner teaching exercise
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Start simple: state in one sentence what the Hypothesis Generation Database tracks.
